stem: Which of the following is the **receiver's response** in the communication process?

options.rationale: Correct: it shows whether the message was understood.
The message is what the sender wants to pass on.
The medium carries the message.
Encoding is how the sender puts the message into words or symbols.

explanation: Feedback is the receiver's response to the message.

stem: Which of these is an example of **written** communication?

options.rationale: Correct: a memo is a written internal message.
A call is spoken communication.
A meeting is spoken communication.
A poster with a chart is visual communication.

explanation: Memos, letters, reports and notices are written methods.

stem: A key advantage of **spoken** communication is that it

options.rationale: Spoken messages leave no record unless written down.
Correct: the receiver can respond or ask questions straight away.

options.content: Reaches many people at no cost
options.rationale: Reaching many people by speech is difficult and costly in time.

options.content: Is always more precise than writing
options.rationale: Writing is usually more precise.

explanation: Spoken communication allows immediate feedback but leaves no record unless notes are taken.

stem: Which method is **most suitable** for giving an employee a formal warning that must be recorded?

options.rationale: A group message is public and impersonal.

options.content: A meeting followed by a written letter
options.rationale: Correct: the meeting allows a response and the letter provides a record.

options.content: A note on the notice board
options.rationale: A public notice breaches confidentiality.

options.content: A passing remark in the corridor
options.rationale: A passing remark is informal and unrecorded.

explanation: Sensitive messages need privacy, feedback and a record.

stem: A fictional wholesaler in Mutare must tell 200 retailers about a price change today. Which method is most suitable?

options.rationale: A personal visit would take too long for 200 retailers.

options.content: Posting a letter to each retailer
options.rationale: The post is slow, so the message would not arrive today.

options.content: Telling the nearest retailer to pass on the message
options.rationale: Passing it on may distort the message or miss retailers.

options.content: A group text message or a group email
options.rationale: Correct: it is fast, cheap and reaches many people at once.

explanation: Electronic communication is fast and cheap for large audiences.
hints: Think about speed and the number of receivers.

stem: A fictional rural clinic supplier in Masvingo wants to advertise a vacancy to people in villages with poor internet access. Which medium is most suitable?

options.rationale: People without the internet cannot see it.
Correct: radio reaches people without internet access.

options.content: An email to the head office
options.rationale: Email would not reach the villagers.
People without internet cannot watch it.

explanation: Radio reaches rural audiences without internet access.
hints: Who needs to receive the message, and what can they access?

stem: Why is **feedback** important in the communication process?

options.rationale: Length is not the aim of feedback.

options.content: It replaces the need for a message
options.rationale: Feedback responds to a message; it does not replace it.

options.content: It removes all barriers to communication
options.rationale: Barriers can still arise.

options.content: It shows whether the message was understood
options.rationale: Correct: the sender can then correct any misunderstanding.

explanation: Without feedback the sender cannot tell whether the message has been understood.
hints: What does the sender need to know?

stem: A fictional factory manager emails a long technical safety procedure to workers who mostly use cell phones with small screens and have limited English. What is the most likely problem?

options.content: Workers will understand better because email is formal
options.rationale: Formality does not help if the receivers cannot read it easily.

options.content: Feedback will be quicker than a meeting
options.rationale: The email provides no immediate feedback.

options.content: The message may not be read or understood
options.rationale: Correct: the medium and language do not suit the receivers.

options.content: The message will automatically be translated
options.rationale: There is no reason to assume translation.

explanation: A method must suit the receiver's equipment and language, otherwise the message is lost.
hints: Think about the receivers, not the sender.

stem: Communication is effective only if the receiver understands the message as the sender intended.
explanation: True. Sending a message is not enough; it must be understood, and feedback shows whether it has been.

stem: A memo is normally used for messages sent from a business to its customers.
explanation: False. A memo is an internal message between people in the same business. A business letter is used for external messages.
hints: Is a memo internal or external?

stem: Match each stage of the communication process to its description.

right.content: The means by which the message is carried
The person for whom the message is intended
The response which shows the message was understood
The person who wants to pass on the message
The information or instruction to be passed on

explanation: Each stage matches one description.

stem: Choose the correct word for each gap.

payload.template: Charts, diagrams and posters are examples of {{blank:a}} communication, whereas email is {{blank:b}} communication.

explanation: Charts and posters are visual; email is electronic.

stem: Name the written internal message between people in the same business, headed To, From, Date and Subject.
explanation: A memorandum (memo) is an internal written message.

stem: A fictional wholesaler in Harare must inform 120 retailers of a change in delivery days. Posting a letter costs US\$0.80 per retailer (printing and postage); a group text message costs US\$0.02 per retailer. How much does the wholesaler save by sending text messages instead of letters?
explanation: Letters: 120 x US\$0.80 = US\$96.00. Texts: 120 x US\$0.02 = US\$2.40. Saving = US\$96.00 - US\$2.40 = US\$93.60. Giving US\$96.00 is the cost of the letters only.
workedSolution: 1. Letters: 120 x US\$0.80 = US\$96.00. Texts: 120 x US\$0.02 = US\$2.40. Saving = US\$96.00 - US\$2.40 = US\$93.60. Giving US\$96.00 is the cost of the letters only.
hints: Find the total cost of each method, then subtract.

stem: A fictional factory holds a half-hour briefing for all 45 workers. Each worker is paid US\$4 an hour. What is the cost of the workers' time for this briefing?
explanation: 45 x 0.5 hours x US\$4 = US\$90. A spoken briefing has a hidden cost in lost production time, even though no equipment is used. Giving US\$180 uses a full hour.
workedSolution:
1. Total hours = 45 x 0.5 = 22.5 hours.
2. Cost = 22.5 x US\$4 = US\$90.
hints: Workers x hours x pay per hour.

stem: Explain why feedback is an important part of the communication process.

points.description: Feedback is the receiver's response to the message
It shows the sender whether the message has been understood
The sender can then correct misunderstandings before mistakes are made

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Feedback is the receiver's response to the message. It shows the sender whether the message has been understood, so the sender can correct misunderstandings before mistakes are made.

explanation: One point per mark.
hints: What does the sender learn from the response?

stem: A fictional hardware shop in Gweru wants to tell staff about a change in the safety rules. Explain **two** reasons why a written notice together with a short staff meeting is better than a notice alone.

points.description: The notice provides a permanent record of the rules
Application: staff can check what the rule says later
The meeting gives immediate feedback
Application: staff can ask questions about using the new equipment

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The notice provides a permanent record, so staff can check later what the rule says. The meeting gives immediate feedback, so staff can ask questions about using the new equipment and the manager can see that they understand.

explanation: Two reasons, each applied to the shop.
hints: Compare the strengths of written and spoken methods.

stem: Analyse how poor communication within a business may harm its performance.

points.description: Instructions may be misunderstood, causing mistakes
Mistakes cause waste and delays
Staff who are not informed feel undervalued, so morale and motivation fall
Customers may be lost if orders are late or wrong

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Instructions may be misunderstood, causing mistakes, waste and delays. Staff who are not informed feel undervalued, so morale and motivation fall. Customers may be lost if orders are late or wrong.

explanation: Mistakes, delay, morale and customers.
hints: Trace the effect from the message to the customer.

stem: Assess whether email is the most suitable method for a fictional manager in Harare to announce a restructuring that may lead to job losses.

points.description: Email is fast and reaches all staff at once
It provides a written record of the announcement
Application: staff in branch offices receive the news at the same time
It is impersonal and gives no immediate feedback for a sensitive message
Staff may hear rumours or feel disrespected if told by email
Judgement with a reason: use face-to-face briefings followed by written confirmation

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Email is fast and reaches all staff at once, including those in branch offices, and provides a written record. But it is impersonal and gives no immediate feedback for a sensitive message, and staff may feel disrespected if told by email. A face-to-face briefing followed by written confirmation is more suitable.

explanation: One point per mark; the judgement needs a reason.
hints: Give a benefit, a limitation and a judgement.

stem: A fictional business: Rudo's Bakery in Mutare employs 20 people. The manager wants to tell all staff that the bakery will close on Monday for repairs. She sends a text message to the staff group at 6 pm on Sunday. On Monday three staff arrive at work because they did not see the message, and one baker had a question about being paid for the day.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: The text message is an example of which method of communication?

options.rationale: A visual method uses charts or diagrams.
A text message is not spoken.
Correct: it is sent by phone.
A text message is not a letter.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain **two** reasons why the communication was not fully effective.

points.description: There was no feedback
Application: the manager did not know whether the staff had read the message
The message was sent at short notice outside working hours
Application: the question on pay was left unanswered, which caused confusion

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: There was no feedback: the manager did not know whether staff had read the message. It was also sent at short notice outside working hours, and the question on pay was left unanswered, which caused confusion.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Suggest **two** ways in which the manager could improve how she communicates a closure in future.

points.description: Give more notice, for example on Friday
Application: staff would have time to arrange their week
Ask staff to confirm that they have read the message
Application: the manager could telephone those who do not reply

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The manager could give more notice, for example on Friday, so staff have time to arrange their week. She could ask staff to confirm that they have read the message and telephone those who do not reply.

explanation: Electronic method; no feedback; more notice and confirmation needed.
hints: Use the five stages of the process model.

stem: A fictional business: Sipho's Mining Supplies in Bulawayo has 80 employees at its head office and in a depot 300 km away. The managing director wants to tell all staff about a new safety procedure that includes diagrams. Past notices on the board were often ignored, and an accident last month happened because a worker did not know the new rule. The depot has poor internet access but staff all have cell phones.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Analyse the factors the managing director should consider in choosing the method of communication.

points.description: Purpose: a safety rule that must be understood and followed
Audience: staff in two places, some without good internet access
Need for diagrams, so a visual element is required
Need for a record that staff have received and understood it
Past notices have been ignored, so feedback is needed

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The purpose is a safety rule that must be understood and followed. The audience is staff in two places, and the depot has poor internet access. The procedure includes diagrams, so a visual element is required. The managing director needs a record that staff have received it and, because notices have been ignored, feedback to show that they have understood.

parts.explanation: Purpose, audience, visual need, record and feedback.
hints: Use purpose, audience, record and feedback.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Evaluate whether the managing director should use printed notices, a group message or face-to-face briefings.

points.description: Printed notices: permanent, can include diagrams; often ignored; no feedback
Group message: fast, cheap and reaches the depot by cell phone; diagrams may be difficult to read; no feedback unless replies are required
Face-to-face briefings: immediate feedback, can demonstrate the procedure; takes time, and the depot is 300 km away so travel or a separate briefing is needed
A combination is likely to be best: briefings, then printed diagrams and a message to confirm
Cost and time of production lost during briefings
Judgement with a reason

levels.descriptor: Weighs the three methods with application to the two sites; justified recommendation with a limitation
Explains methods with some application; judgement weak

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Printed notices are permanent and can include diagrams, but they have often been ignored and give no feedback. A group message is fast and cheap and reaches the depot by cell phone, but diagrams may be hard to read on small screens and it gives no feedback unless replies are required. Face-to-face briefings allow immediate feedback and a demonstration, but they take time and the depot is 300 km away. A combination is likely to be best: briefings at each site led by a supervisor, followed by printed diagrams and a group message asking staff to confirm they have understood. Given the recent accident, the extra cost of lost working time is justified.

parts.explanation: Compare methods, then recommend a combination.
hints: Weigh the strengths and weaknesses of each method against safety and distance.

explanation: A combination of briefings, printed diagrams and a confirming message.
hints: Think about feedback, diagrams and the distance between sites.
